title: Trachea and bronchial tree (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Location
Runs from the cricoid cartilage at C6 to its division into the two main bronchi at the level of the sternal angle. The esophagus lies behind it.
Function
Carries air to and from the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage hold it open, and the gap at the back is closed by the trachealis muscle.
hy: In the most common form of tracheoesophageal fistula the upper esophagus ends blindly and the lower esophagus opens into the trachea; the newborn drools, chokes and turns blue with the first feed.

rows: Location
Runs from the division of the trachea, at the level of the sternal angle, to the hilum of the right lung.
Features
It is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left main bronchus.
hy: Inhaled objects and fluids enter the right lung more often than the left because of the shape and direction of this bronchus.

rows: Location
Runs from the division of the trachea to the hilum of the left lung, passing under the aortic arch and in front of the esophagus.
Features
It is narrower, longer and more horizontal than the right main bronchus.
Location
Leaves the right main bronchus before it enters the lung, above the right pulmonary artery.
Supplies
Superior lobe of the right lung, through apical, posterior and anterior segmental bronchi.
Location
The right main bronchus beyond the origin of the superior lobar bronchus.
Supplies
Divides into the middle lobar and right inferior lobar bronchi.
Location
Leaves the front of the intermediate bronchus.
Supplies
Middle lobe of the right lung, through lateral and medial segmental bronchi.
Location
Continues the intermediate bronchus beyond the origin of the middle lobar bronchus.
Supplies
Inferior lobe of the right lung, through a superior and four basal segmental bronchi.
Location
Leaves the left main bronchus inside the hilum of the left lung.
Supplies
Superior lobe of the left lung, including the lingula.
Location
Continues the left main bronchus beyond the origin of the superior lobar bronchus.
Supplies
Inferior lobe of the left lung, through a superior and three basal segmental bronchi.
Location
Largest cartilage of the larynx, at the level of C4 to C5. Its two plates meet in front at the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
Function
Shields the front of the larynx. The vocal ligaments attach to the back of the angle between its plates, and its inferior horns hinge on the cricoid cartilage.
Location
Below the thyroid cartilage at the level of C6, where the larynx becomes the trachea and the pharynx becomes the esophagus. It is shaped like a signet ring, narrow in front and tall behind.
Function
Forms the base of the larynx and carries the arytenoid cartilages. It is the only complete ring of cartilage in the airway.
Location
Front of the neck at the level of C3, between the mandible and the larynx. It is U-shaped.
Articulates with
No other bone. It is held in place by muscles and ligaments, with the thyrohyoid membrane joining it to the larynx.
Features
Body with greater and lesser horns. It anchors the tongue and the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles.
hy: A fractured hyoid in an adult suggests strangulation.
